meta.description: Alpha and beta diversity of an amplicon (16S/ITS) ASV/OTU community table: observed features, Shannon, Pielou evenness, Faith PD, Bray-Curtis, Jaccard, weighted/unweighted/generalized UniFrac, Aitchison/RPCA, via QIIME2 core-metrics-phylogenetic, phyloseq/vegan, and scikit-bio, with PERMANOVA paired with betadisper.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 12 references (Faith 1992, Pielou 1966, Lozupone 2005/2007, Chen 2012, Janssen 2018, Mirarab 2012, McDonald 2018/2024, Martino 2019, McMurdie 2013/2014, Schloss 2024) are real, verifiable, well-known papers in this exact literature. No fabricated statistics, p-values, or effect sizes anywhere in the Skill.

practice_boundaries.detail: Community-level microbiome diversity statistics for research use; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about individuals anywhere; no medical disclaimer required for this scope.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill actively prevents methodological fallacies for the cases it covers: explicit, verified-correct warnings against rarefying to min(sample_sums), against reusing the rarefied table for differential abundance, and mandatory betadisper pairing with every PERMANOVA (confirmed necessary on both a synthetic fixture and a real dataset, where dispersion confounds were genuinely present). One real gap found and recorded as a P1, not a veto: the Beta Diversity/PERMANOVA section gives no guidance for repeated-measures/pseudo-replicated designs, unlike the parallel Alpha Diversity section. Tested on a real longitudinal fixture, a naive pooled PERMANOVA (p=0.098) did not flip the qualitative conclusion relative to a properly restricted one (p=1), so no output actually committed a reporting fallacy in this audit -- but the gap is real and would matter on a different draw.

code_usability.detail: All real R code (fixture-based alpha/beta/PERMANOVA/betadisper, the verbatim SKILL.md generalized-UniFrac line) and the full real QIIME2 2024.10.1 CLI pipeline (import through core-metrics-phylogenetic and beta-group-significance) executed successfully across all 7 inputs and a second independent real dataset. One bundled demo script (examples/diversity_analysis.R) crashed with 'object Group not found' due to a variable-naming copy-paste bug; a one-line fix (verified) fully resolves it. Recorded as a P1, not a veto, since it is a bundled demo artifact, not the SKILL.md prose pattern itself (which was independently exercised and confirmed correct throughout).

functional_suitability.note: Completeness: thorough coverage of alpha (Observed/Shannon/Pielou/Faith PD), beta (Bray-Curtis/Jaccard/weighted+unweighted+generalized UniFrac), tree-building (SEPP vs de novo) and PERMANOVA+betadisper; gaps are NMDS (never mentioned) and RPCA (named in the Tool Taxonomy/Decision Tree but only a one-line CLI reference, no worked code). Correctness: verified accurate by real execution end to end; one shipped example (examples/diversity_analysis.R) crashes on its own demo data (real, reproducible, one-line fix confirmed). Appropriateness: excellent -- the three-knobs framing (depth/tree/metric) is exactly right and directly validated by real dispersion-confound findings on two independent datasets.

reliability.note: Fault tolerance: the Common Errors and Per-Method Failure Modes tables anticipate and correctly describe every real failure mode this audit triggered (no-tree UniFrac error, sampling-depth sample loss, Shannon base mismatch, PERMANOVA dispersion), but give no guidance for repeated-measures/pseudo-replicated PERMANOVA designs (a real gap found via the longitudinal fixture). Error reporting is clear and specific throughout (the tree-less UniFrac error matches the documented message exactly). Recoverability is generally strong (fixed seeds, one-line fixes) but the shipped-example bug would confuse a first-time user before self-diagnosis.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is 223 lines (well under the 500-line guideline), with usage-guide.md and examples/ split out for progressive disclosure; dense but well-organized tables keep it efficient to scan.

agent_usability.note: Very high learnability -- all 7 real test inputs were completed cold-start using only SKILL.md's stated patterns with no need to guess. Minor consistency gap: the Alpha and Beta Diversity R code blocks build the grouping-variable dataframe in slightly different styles. Feedback design and error prevention are both excellent, backed by a detailed Common Errors / Per-Method Failure Modes section that matched real observed behavior throughout.

human_usability.note: Description frontmatter and usage-guide Quick Start use natural trigger phrasing ('Compare microbial diversity across my samples') that matches how a researcher would actually ask. Forgiveness is solid (graceful non-phylogenetic fallback, confirmed working) with only the repeated-measures gap as a soft spot.

security.note: No credentials, no unsanitized execution of user-provided strings, no sensitive-data handling concerns for community-level microbiome data.

maintainability.note: Clean separation between SKILL.md (reference), usage-guide.md (prompts/quickstart) and examples/ (runnable scripts). Testability is docked one point because the one shipped 'test case' example is itself broken as-is.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger boundaries (per-taxon -> differential-abundance; shotgun tables -> metagenome-visualization), confirmed by a clean real redirect in Input 6. Strong progressive disclosure, clear Related Skills composability, fully seeded/deterministic pipeline, and explicit escape hatches (anti-min-depth warning, DA/diversity separation) all verified in real execution.

key_strengths: Real execution across two independent datasets (a 40-sample phyloseq fixture and QIIME2's real moving-pictures 16S tutorial dataset) confirms every core numeric claim: min(sample_sums) rarefaction under-saturates richness by ~18%, weighted/unweighted/generalized UniFrac interpolate exactly as documented, and the sampling-depth silent-drop behavior reproduces on both datasets.

The mandatory PERMANOVA+betadisper pairing is demonstrably necessary, not just documented: on both the R fixture and the real body-site dataset, beta metrics turned out to be dispersion-confounded, and the Skill's own guidance correctly anticipates and instructs how to report this.

Clean, correctly-enforced scope boundaries: per-taxon requests redirect to differential-abundance, min(sample_sums) anti-pattern requests get a quantified pushback rather than blind compliance, and a tree-less input falls back to non-phylogenetic metrics with a clear documented error rather than a silent wrong answer.

This Skill's own data.frame(sample_data(ps)) pattern (SKILL.md and the shipped example) is verified NOT to hit the as.data.frame() S4-class coercion trap that broke the sibling differential-abundance Skill's LinDA code on the identical fixture object.

recommendations.title: Shipped example script crashes on its own demo data
recommendations.problem: examples/diversity_analysis.R crashes with "object 'Group' not found" at the adonis2 call because meta <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_rare)) never receives a Group column -- only the separate alpha data.frame does (alpha$Group <- sample_data(ps_rare)$SampleType).
recommendations.root_cause: Copy-paste oversight: the demo script's grouping-variable name ('Group') doesn't match GlobalPatterns' real column name ('SampleType'), and the fix applied to alpha was never mirrored onto meta.
recommendations.fix: Add meta$Group <- sample_data(ps_rare)$SampleType immediately after the meta <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_rare)) line; verified this one-line fix fully resolves the crash and the script runs to completion.

recommendations.title: No repeated-measures/pseudo-replication guidance for beta diversity
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's Alpha Diversity section says to escalate to lme4/nlme for repeated measures, but the Beta Diversity/PERMANOVA section and its code block never mention non-independence or vegan's strata= argument. On a real 3-visits-per-subject fixture, a naive pooled PERMANOVA gives p=0.098 (borderline) while a properly restricted analysis (strata=SubjectID) gives p=1 (no signal).
recommendations.root_cause: The Beta Diversity in R section's adonis2 pattern has no repeated-measures branch or warning, unlike the parallel alpha-diversity section.
recommendations.fix: Add a repeated-measures note to the Beta Diversity section mirroring the alpha-diversity one: when samples are nested within subjects/repeated over time, use adonis2(..., strata = SubjectID) and warn that pooling all timepoints without restriction inflates apparent significance.

recommendations.title: NMDS and RPCA are named but not backed by worked code
recommendations.problem: The Skill documents PCoA thoroughly (R and QIIME2) but never mentions NMDS at all, and RPCA/DEICODE appears only as a one-line CLI reference with no worked R/Python example, despite being listed in the Tool Taxonomy and Decision Tree.
recommendations.root_cause: Progressive disclosure stopped one level short for these two secondary methods.
recommendations.fix: Add a short NMDS snippet (vegan::metaMDS) alongside the PCoA one, and either a worked RPCA example or an explicit note routing to qiime2-workflow for the full deicode/gemelli command.
